questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country needed to differ from Danish culture, while still being quite modern and a well-functioning society. That the destination was acknowledged for high qualitity education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I 100% reccommend going on exchange in Seoul, one of my best and most meaningful decisions in my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As I remember, the information was okay to find. The host university website can be a bit confusing to navigate. I feel like there were a lot of small things i did not know before arrving, but the most important information is easily communicated from the university and host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. There was a welcoming ceremony. You can assign a buddy-program, your buddy will then give you a tour of the campus and invite you to optional gatherings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: EWHA international office is super super helpfull with any questions, so dont hesitate to reach out to them.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite okay I lived with another Dane. We found our apartment through Enkostay, which works like Airbnb but is cheaper.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will most likely not use the kitchen as it is impossible and expensive to grocery shop, so don't choose your apartment from this. Find a small but nice cheap place, you will not be spending much time at home, but its nice to have something that works.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My apartment where super old and scrappy, we almost only slept there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, an essay process, but it is very long, and the deadlines never end. But if you are mentally prepared for this, it will be okay.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I dont remeber it so well. There is a lot of paper work, but both universities are helpful in this process. But be patient as it might take some time to get the documents from KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As written earlier, both universities will help and guide you. EWHA sends out a lot of emails about deadlines, so you will not miss these. You just need to be patient as a lot of the deadlines are during summer (so a bit late)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got 1/5 classes on my first priority. The process is a first come first serve basis (online). There a lot of competition on some classes which was why I ended up with some random ones, that i did not plan for. Unforturnatly there is not much to do about this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared with second and third choices course and prepare your self so you dont get disapointed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very frustrated with the Korean university system; it is very traditional, with attendance, a lot of assignments, etc. All my exams where closed book, handwritten sit-ins, which were very different from other exams at KU. Some of my profs talked Korean for some parts of the class even though it was an English thought class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The engineering classes were crazy difficult and high demanding - while my other classes were easier than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As stated earlier it is very traditional

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Computer Architecture, Blockchain Application, International Politics, Gender relations in Korea, Feminist education theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed International Politics

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive to cook, so you eat out for every meal, and even though it is cheaper then copenhagen it adds up for every meal.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is generally cheaper than copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any of these so i have no say to this.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside Seoul at the weekends, Korea has so much to offer!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The first few days were overstimulating but i have really felt save and at home in Seoul.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did get any Korean friends, so dont expect this.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Social manners are a bit different, they don't hold the door, they don't give room at the sidewalk etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness and coolness. Food!! and coffee

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be excited for the best experience in your life, pack light as you want to by everything, you will make friends!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about deadlines beforehand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my family and friends. The school system was quite challenging

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
